facts.text: Tazlina’s name comes from the Ahtna Athabascan word meaning 'swift water,' reflecting the river’s rapid flow.
Before becoming a permanent village in 1900, Tazlina was a seasonal fishing camp for migrating Ahtna Athabascan tribes.
At the confluence of the Tazlina and Copper Rivers, braided channels and glacial outwash plains shape the local landscape.
Much of the Copper River Basin, including Tazlina, sits on discontinuous permafrost, raising ground stability concerns and increasing wildfire risk during dry, windy summers.
Archaeological and oral evidence shows the Ahtna people have inhabited the Tazlina area for roughly 5,000 years.
South of Tazlina, the Chugach Mountains rise to over 7,000 feet, influencing local drainage and providing a dramatic backdrop.
